connections.why: The variety of organisms is grouped by shared characteristics of life
Membrane structure controls what moves into and out of cells
Enzymes digest the biological molecules in food
Photosynthesis and digestion supply the glucose respiration uses
Transport systems deliver oxygen and glucose to respiring cells
Blood carries the wastes excreted and the hormones that coordinate the body
Sexual reproduction passes genes from parents to offspring
Selective breeding and genetic modification manipulate inherited genes
Understanding photosynthesis underpins efficient crop production
Human activity disrupts feeding relationships and cycles
Food production manages ecosystems for higher yield
Cell division produces the gametes used in reproduction
Molecule size and solubility determine how substances cross membranes
Inherited variation, over time, produces the variety of organisms
